ai.description: *Raorchestes sushili* is a small bushfrog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum, cream-colored venter, and distinct reddish-brown iris. It features a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes sushili* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes sushili inhabits the mid-to-high altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Sushil's Bushfrog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden among dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes sushili* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes sushili is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes sushili* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation forests.
